_about: Ships by class and navy, the card side (Brian's ask of 22 November 2026, 04:03Z; the design director's rulings of 08:49Z and 11:09Z on the naval thread's plan v3, naval-battles/ships-by-class-plan.md). A class's worth is the square root of its gunfire times its armour, each against a yardstick: F, the kilograms of shell a minute (guns x rounds a minute x shell kg), against 12,240; P, the square root of its thickest belt plate times its thickest deck plate, against the square root of 305 x 127 (Q1, Q2). The yardstick is the median of the seven 1939-41 newest classes. Worths are rebased per kind so that the fleets at the start of a campaign keep their total (src/campaign/shiprows.ts rebase). Off unless the campaign carries the flag 'shipRows' (data/campaign/stage.json 'shipRows'): off, nothing here is read.
_marks: Marks as the record gives them: H, M, L the historian's; r recalled (UNCONFIRMED); W a web figure read by the naval thread's re-verify, not yet in the record. A row with 'worth' and no inputs is one whose inputs the record already holds (record sections 2 and 3) but which the naval thread worked out from them (its check-numbers.py); the inputs are to be copied here when the historian's 1939 pass lands.

steps._about: The record's periods (plan 4.2). A step is held by research only, never by a date: step 1 with 'firecontrol', step 2 with 'taskforces' (tech.json), in the grand campaign. A history campaign keeps no research tree, and builds no battleships. Route 2 (Q4): a navy builds its own best row of the steps it holds, lifted to the step's median once it holds step 1 or 2. 'periods' are the rows whose median is the step's: steps 0 and 1 the seven navies, step 2 six (Italy leaves the record's table after September 1943).
